data.source_title: An Observational Study of the Factors Affecting Staffing Demands During Intrahospital Transfers
data.locator: Methods (observed transfer definition); Results and Table 3. Observation ended when origin nurse returned to origin unit.
data.source_setting: 718-bed Level I trauma hospital; 39 between-unit and 11 within-unit transfers observed, including ICU/PCU transfers.
data.source_period: Publication 2025; observation dates/collection window not specified in the accessible full text.
data.source_n: 50 complete observed transfers; 5 additional observations excluded for discontinuity or destination change; 7 pilot observations not included.
data.quantity: Mean total transfer-related staff time and RN time per observed transfer
data.unit: minutes of staff labor per transfer (means)
data.source_evidence_basis: Direct structured observation summed staff time spent on transfer-related tasks. The study notes that total staff labor can exceed elapsed transfer time because multiple people work simultaneously.
data.limitations: Small convenience observation sample at a trauma hospital, principally daytime; staff labor minutes are not elapsed patient journey duration. The value is a mean, not a distribution or universal transfer-time estimate.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use as an external labor-demand anchor for transfer episodes, keeping staff-minutes distinct from patient elapsed time. Represent acuity changes, equipment/belongings setup, handoff, destination readiness, and elevator use as transition/resource factors.

data.source_title: An Observational Study of the Factors Affecting Staffing Demands During Intrahospital Transfers
data.locator: Table 3 (activity time means and SDs); Results (elevator-use stratification).
data.source_setting: Same 718-bed Level I trauma hospital observed intrahospital transfers.
data.source_period: Observation dates/collection window not specified in accessible full text; article published 2025.
data.source_n: Activity denominators vary: patient transport n=50; elevator/no-elevator regression subgroup counts not stated in Results passage.
data.quantity: Observed transport-with-patient task and total staff-time by elevator use
data.unit: minutes; task mean (SD) and total staff-time means stratified by elevator use
data.source_evidence_basis: Table 3 reports mean staff time to move the patient from room to destination room. A regression analysis in Results reports higher mean total staff and nurse labor when an elevator was used.
data.limitations: Transport task time is one subtask and is not the full transfer. Elevator figures are staff labor means, not elapsed trip time; subgroup denominators are not reported in the cited Results passage. Small single-hospital sample; no distribution inference.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Separate moving time from room preparation, handoff, setup, return tasks, and staff labor. Use elevator as a context-sensitive factor to test, not a universal fixed multiplier or RWJ-specific estimate.
